message.content:
When you toss three fair coins, each coin has two equally‑likely outcomes (heads or tails).  
With three independent flips there are \(2^3 = 8\) equally likely sequences:

| Sequence | Heads |
|----------|-------|
| HHH      | 3     |
| HHT      | 2     |
| HTH      | 2     |
| THH      | 2     |
| HTT      | 1     |
| THT      | 1     |
| TTH      | 1     |
| TTT      | 0     |

So the **possible numbers of heads** you can observe are:

* 0 heads – probability \(1/8\)
* 1 head  – probability \(3/8\)
* 2 heads – probability \(3/8\)
* 3 heads – probability \(1/8\)

In other words, after tossing three coins you can get anywhere from 0 up to 3 heads (inclusive).
